findings.title: Activity newest-first ordering is not pinned by a single-payment test
findings.failure_scenario: Change `state.activity.insert(payment, at: 0)` to `state.activity.append(payment)` at AppFeature.swift:81. sendFlow starts from AppFeature.State() with activity == [], so after one send activity is [payment] either way and the exhaustive TestStore assertion `$0.activity = [payment]` still passes. The history would then list oldest first, breaking the 'newest first' doc comment at AppFeature.swift:19, and no test fails. The test name's claim 'heads activity' is never checked.
findings.evidence: AppFeatureTests.swift:58 `TestStore(initialState: AppFeature.State())` (activity defaults to []), line 69 `$0.activity = [payment]`. AppFeature.swift:81 `state.activity.insert(payment, at: 0)`. AppFeature.swift:19 `/// Sent payments, newest first.`
findings.fix: Start from State(activity: [earlierPayment]) or run two sends. Assert the second payment is at index 0 and the balance is reduced by both amounts.
findings.verification_note: Read AppFeature.swift and AppFeatureTests.swift in the worktree. sendFlow starts with empty activity and sends one payment, so the expected [payment] is the same under insert-at-0 and append. The mutation survives, so the claim holds. I lowered the severity from major to minor because the production code is correct today (it inserts at 0). The harm is a regression the test would miss, not a wrong outcome any user hits now.

findings.title: No test for a non-SendError failure or a repeat tap while sending
findings.failure_scenario: Case 1: delete the generic `catch { await send(.sendResponse(.failure(.declined))) }` at ConfirmFeature.swift:54-56. The .run closure can throw, so the code still compiles. A non-SendError from accountClient.send then escapes the effect, sendResponse is never sent, and isSending stays true. Both tests still pass because they only throw SendError.declined or succeed. Case 2: the reducer at ConfirmFeature.swift:44-57 has no isSending guard, so a second sendButtonTapped while a send is in flight starts a second accountClient.send. No test covers this.
findings.evidence: ConfirmFeature.swift:44 `case .sendButtonTapped, .retryButtonTapped:` sets isSending = true with no guard. Lines 52-56 handle `catch let error as SendError` and then a generic `catch`. ConfirmFeatureTests.swift has only sendSucceeds (success) and failThenRetry (SendError.declined, then success).
findings.fix: Add a test where accountClient.send throws a non-SendError and expect error == .declined. Add a test that a second sendButtonTapped during isSending triggers no second send call. Add a guard in the reducer if that behavior is intended.
findings.verification_note: Read ConfirmFeature.swift and ConfirmFeatureTests.swift. Neither test throws a non-SendError, so the generic catch branch never runs and deleting it would leave both tests green. The reducer has no isSending guard, and no test sends a second tap while a send is in flight. The view is not in the write set, so I could not check whether it disables the button while sending. Minor fits: this is a missing edge-case test with no wrong outcome today. The second scenario is partly a product question (should a tap during sending be ignored?), not only a test gap.

notes:
AppFeature: filteredContacts is a case-insensitive substring match (all when empty); .task loads balance and contacts then sends .accountLoaded; contactTapped pushes .amount; amount delegate .continued pushes .confirm; confirm delegate .sent lowers balance, inserts payment at activity[0] and clears the path. ConfirmFeature: sendButtonTapped and retryButtonTapped set isSending, clear error, call accountClient.send; a non-SendError thrown maps to .declined; failure logs "send failed" (category "send") via LogClient. Added AppFeatureTests and ConfirmFeatureTests (7 tests in all). The slice gate ran with prove. The plan listed no test ids.
